Several bugs stemmed from caches (model catalogs, file contents, diffs, generated media) not being invalidated when the underlying data changed — switching accounts kept a stale model list, downloading/deleting a model left the old catalog cached, and file/diff caches kept showing content from before an external edit or git action. Whenever a cache's source of truth can change — via a user action (switch account, delete, discard), an external event (file edited outside the app, git state change), or a background mutation — the cache must be invalidated as part of that change, not left to accidentally expire or be manually refreshed.

Prefer marking affected entries stale and re-fetching in the background over clearing them outright: clearing causes UI flicker (spinners popping in on every poll) while marking-stale lets the UI keep showing the last-known value until the fresh one arrives. Compare content/snapshot identity rather than counts alone, since two changes can leave a count-based signature unchanged while content differs.

Because invalidation triggers an async refetch, guard against races with a per-key generation/version counter so a slow, now-stale in-flight request can't overwrite a result from a newer request:

```ts
const generationRef = useRef(new Map<string, number>());

function invalidate(key: string) {
  generationRef.current.set(key, (generationRef.current.get(key) ?? 0) + 1);
}

async function read(key: string) {
  const generation = (generationRef.current.get(key) ?? 0) + 1;
  generationRef.current.set(key, generation);
  const result = await fetchData(key);
  if (generationRef.current.get(key) !== generation) return; // stale, discard
  applyResult(key, result);
}
```

For caches that persist derived artifacts (e.g. materialized files from repeated content), key entries by a content hash so identical inputs are deduped instead of regenerated, and clear the cache alongside any backing storage on teardown/exit.
